about: The commands, shortcuts and settings of the VS Code extension (its package.json).

rows.title: VS Code: the commands of the Nuclear extension and their shortcuts
rows.summary: The 72 commands the Nuclear extension adds to VS Code, each with its keyboard shortcut: the workspace, run and debug, devices, the HTTP tool, the Loop, the agent's chat and the settings.
body: - Run an Action of the Active Project (run, debug, build, test…) (`nuclear.workspace.action`)
- Add the Active Project to the VS Code Workspace (`nuclear.workspace.addToVsCode`)
- Welcome Page — `ctrl+alt+w` (`nuclear.workspace.welcome`)
- Set Up the AI Services (`nuclear.ai.setup`)

- Open a Tool — `ctrl+alt+h (arg http), ctrl+alt+p (arg loop), ctrl+alt+d (arg designer), ctrl+alt+m (arg docs), ctrl+alt+a (arg agent), ctrl+alt+s (arg settings), ctrl+alt+v (arg devices)` (`nuclear.workspace.tool`)
- Open a Project as a Tab — `ctrl+alt+o` (`nuclear.workspace.openProject`)
- Go to Project Tab — `ctrl+1 (arg 1), ctrl+2 (arg 2), ctrl+3 (arg 3), ctrl+4 (arg 4), ctrl+5 (arg 5), ctrl+6 (arg 6), ctrl+7 (arg 7), ctrl+8 (arg 8), ctrl+9 (arg 9)` (`nuclear.workspace.project`)
- Show the Nuclear Workspace — `ctrl+alt+n` (`nuclear.workspace.show`)
- Refresh (`nuclear.http.refresh`)
- Select Environment (`nuclear.http.selectEnvironment`)
- Edit Environments (variables, headers, base urls) (`nuclear.http.editEnvironments`)
- Add an OpenAPI Document (`nuclear.http.addOpenApi`)
- Open Request (`nuclear.http.open`)
- Update Contracts (nuclear contracts update) (`nuclear.contracts.update`)
- Run (`nuclear.run`)
- Debug (`nuclear.debug`)
- Show Generated Code (`nuclear.showGeneratedCode`)
- Select Dialect (`nuclear.selectDialect`)
- Restart Language Server (`nuclear.restartServer`)
- Toggle code lenses for arrow functions (`nuclear.toggleCodeMetricsForArrowFunctions`)
- Toggle code metrics (`nuclear.toggleCodeMetricsDisplayed`)
- Show code metrics details (`nuclear.showCodeMetricsCodeLensInfo`)
- Open Dragonfly Device (`nuclear.openDevice`)
- Run on Dragonfly Device (`nuclear.runOnDevice`)
- Step Over (Nuclear Line) — `f10` (`nuclear.debug.stepOver`)
- Step Into (Nuclear Line) — `f11` (`nuclear.debug.stepInto`)
- Step Out (Nuclear) — `shift+f11` (`nuclear.debug.stepOut`)
- Go to the Same Line in Nuclear / Dart (`nuclear.debug.otherSide`)
- Open Frame (`nuclear.debug.openPlace`)
- Run — `ctrl+alt+r` (`nuclear.action.run`)
- Serve — `ctrl+alt+r` (`nuclear.action.serve`)
- Debug — `ctrl+alt+g` (`nuclear.action.debug`)
- Hot Reload — `ctrl+alt+l` (`nuclear.action.reload`)
- Run on a Dragonfly Device (`nuclear.action.device`)
- Build — `ctrl+alt+b` (`nuclear.action.build`)
- Test — `ctrl+alt+t` (`nuclear.action.test`)

rows.title: VS Code: the settings of the Nuclear extension for the AI loop, the local agents and their integrations
rows.summary: The 30 settings of the Nuclear extension for the AI loop, the local agents and their integrations, with their defaults.
body: - `nuclear.ai.developerUrl` (default `"http://127.0.0.1:7879"`): Where the Nuclear Developer (the local agents) answers.
- `nuclear.ai.graphUrl` (default `"http://127.0.0.1:7878"`): Where the Nuclear Smart Graph answers.
- `nuclear.ai.ollamaUrl` (default `"http://localhost:11434"`): Where Ollama runs the local models.

- `nuclear.ai.models.coder` (default `"qwen2.5-coder:3b"`): The local model that writes and repairs code and tests (at most 3B parameters). Applies when the Developer is started from Settings and integrations.
- `nuclear.ai.models.assistant` (default `"gemma4:e2b"`): The local model that plans, reviews, documents, diagnoses and chats (at most 3B effective parameters).
- `nuclear.ai.models.embeddings` (default `"embeddinggemma"`): The embeddings model of the Smart Graph's search (re-ingest after changing it).
- `nuclear.ai.claudeModel` (default `"sonnet"`): Claude's model when Claude leads a Loop run.
- `nuclear.ai.mcpCommand` (default `"nuclear-graph"`): The program that serves the Nuclear MCP server (`<command> mcp`) and the graph.
- `nuclear.ai.retry.attempts` (default `5`): Tries of a call to the local agents that fails for a passing reason (down, busy, 5xx), the first included.
- `nuclear.ai.retry.baseMs` (default `1000`): The ceiling of the first wait before a retry, in milliseconds; it doubles at each retry (exponential backoff with full jitter).
- `nuclear.ai.retry.maxMs` (default `30000`): The longest wait before a retry, in milliseconds.

- `nuclear.ai.contextTokens` (default `8192`): The context window of the local models, in tokens: what the chat's meter measures against. The Nuclear Developer runs its models with 8192 (config/project_config.nuc numCtx).
- `nuclear.ai.claude.command` (default `"claude"`): Claude Code's command: the Loop's lead when Claude leads, checked before every such run.
- `nuclear.ai.claude.maxBudgetUsd` (default `2`): The most a Loop run led by Claude may spend, in USD (0: no limit).
- `nuclear.ai.codex.enabled` (default `false`): Use Codex (its MCP server entry and its regular check).
- `nuclear.ai.codex.command` (default `"codex"`): Codex's command.
- `nuclear.ai.opencode.enabled` (default `false`): Use OpenCode (its MCP server entry and its regular check).
- `nuclear.ai.opencode.command` (default `"opencode"`): OpenCode's command.
- `nuclear.ai.opencode.configFile` (default `"~/.config/opencode/opencode.json"`): OpenCode's configuration file, where the Nuclear MCP server is added.
- `nuclear.ai.cursor.mcpFile` (default `"~/.cursor/mcp.json"`): Cursor's MCP configuration file, where the Nuclear MCP server is added.
- `nuclear.ai.github.command` (default `"gh"`): GitHub's command line (issues imported as Loop specs), checked with `gh auth status`.
- `nuclear.ai.jira.site` (default `""`): Your Jira site (https://your-team.atlassian.net): issues imported as Loop specs. The API token is kept in the secret storage.
- `nuclear.ai.jira.email` (default `""`): The email of your Atlassian account (Jira).
- `nuclear.ai.jira.criteriaField` (default `""`): Optional: the Jira field that holds the acceptance criteria (customfield_10050); empty: read them from the description.
- `nuclear.ai.watch.callTimeoutMinutes` (default `15`): A call to the local agents that takes longer is cut and retried.
- `nuclear.ai.watch.stallSeconds` (default `90`): A call is stalled (cut and retried) when, this long, the Developer does not answer or Ollama holds no model.
- `nuclear.ai.watch.minFreeMb` (default `500`): Free disk space (the project and the temporary folder) a Loop run needs before it starts.
- `nuclear.ai.resumeInterrupted` (default `true`): A Loop run the editor left half done (closed or crashed) is recovered and goes on from the step where it stopped.

- `nuclear.ai.checkEveryMinutes` (default `5`): How often every connection (the Developer, the Smart Graph, Ollama and its models, Claude, Codex, OpenCode, GitHub, Jira) is checked; a notification says when one stops answering (0: only before each task).
- `nuclear.ai.watch.commandTimeoutMinutes` (default `20`): A command of the Loop (a build, the tests) that runs longer is killed with its children and the step fails.

rows.title: VS Code: the settings of the Nuclear extension for the language, the dialect, the build and the devices
rows.summary: The 113 settings of the Nuclear extension for the language, the dialect, the build and the devices, with their defaults.
body: - `nuclear.dialect` (default `"flutter"`): Dialect used to check `.nuc` files outside a project. A project names its platform and dialect in `config.nuc` (or `nuclear.toml`) and the server uses those. `base` checks only the base language.
- `nuclear.dialectPaths` (default `[]`): Extra directories with dialects (absolute or relative to the workspace). `<workspace>/dialects` is always searched.
- `nuclear.server.path` (default `""`): Path to the `nuclear-lsp` binary. Empty: the one bundled with the extension, then `nuclear-lsp` on the `PATH`.
- `nuclear.trace.server` (default `"off"`): Traces the communication between VS Code and the Nuclear language server.
- `nuclear.debug.followInNuclear` (default `true`): When a Dragonfly app pauses (breakpoint, step, exception), show and highlight the .nuc line of the paused code.

- `nuclear.debug.explainErrors` (default `true`): Show Dart run-time errors of a Dragonfly app at their .nuc line (Problems panel) with a panel beside that explains the error, the Nuclear call stack and the original Dart error.
- `nuclear.workspace.welcome` (default `true`): Show the Nuclear workspace welcome page (projects and shortcuts) when VS Code starts with no editor open. Ctrl+Alt+W opens it any time.

- `nuclear.buildOnSave` (default `true`): Saving a `.nuc` of a backend or web project runs `dragonfly build`: the running server or page reloads by itself (uvicorn `--reload`, `node --watch`, Vite). Mobile projects hot reload on save through the Flutter session.
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.CodeLensEnabled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown as code lens
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.CodeLensHiddenUnder` (default `3`): Threshold to show code lens for code metrics
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorExtreme` (default `"#ff0000"`): Color for the extreme complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorHigh` (default `"#f44034"`): Color for the high complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorLow` (default `"#4bb14f"`): Color for the low complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityColorNormal` (default `"#ffc208"`): Color for the normal complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelExtreme` (default `25`): Threshold to determine extreme high complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelExtremeDescription` (default `"Bloody hell..."`): Code lens message for extreme high complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelHigh` (default `10`): Threshold to determine high complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelHighDescription` (default `"You must be kidding"`): Code lens message for high complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelLow` (default `0`): Threshold to determine low complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelLowDescription` (default `"Everything is cool!"`): Code lens message for low complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelNormal` (default `5`): Threshold to determine normal complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityLevelNormalDescription` (default `"It's time to do something..."`): Code lens message for normal complexity level
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.ComplexityTemplate` (default `"Complexity is {0} {1}"`): Code lens message template {0} stands for the actual value {1} is for the complexity level description
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.DecorationModeEnabled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown as inline decoration

- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.DecorationTemplate` (default `"<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='{{size}}px' height='{{size}}px' viewbox='0 0 {{size}} {{size}}'><rect width='{{size}}' height='{{size}}' style='fill:{{color}};stroke-width:1;stroke:#fff'/></svg>"`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown as inline decoration
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.DiagnosticsEnabled` (default `false`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown as diagnostics
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.Exclude` (default `[]`): Array of exclusion patterns (in glob format)
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.FileSizeLimitMB` (default `0.5`): File size limit in megabytes, above this codemetrics are not going to be computed, use a negative number to allow any size
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.IgnoredFunctionNames` (default `[]`): A set of function names to ignore from calculations
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.MetricsForArrowFunctionsToggled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for arrow functions (can also be toggled via a command)
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.MetricsForClassDeclarationsToggled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for class declarations
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.MetricsForConstructorsToggled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for constructors
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.MetricsForEnumDeclarationsToggled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for enum declarations
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.MetricsForFunctionDeclarationsToggled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for function declarations
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.MetricsForFunctionExpressionsToggled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for function expressions
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.MetricsForMethodDeclarationsToggled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are enabled for methods declarations
- `nuclear.codemetrics.basics.OverviewRulerModeEnabled` (default `true`): A flag which indicates whether code metrics are shown on the overview ruler
- `nuclear.codemetrics.nodeconfiguration.ArrayLiteralExpression` (default `0`): Complexity increment of list literal `[a, b]`
- `nuclear.codemetrics.nodeconfiguration.ArrayLiteralExpressionDescription` (default `"Array literal expression"`): Text of list literal `[a, b]` in the details list
